statement: For H(3,3)=K_3 square K_3 square K_3 on [3]^3, with adjacency defined by differing in exactly one coordinate and with surjective weak-majority C-colorings requiring at least three same-color neighbors at every vertex, the maximum possible number of colors is 4: bar_chi_>=(H(3,3))=4.
contribution: Complete elementary proof of both bounds. Every qualifying color class has at least six vertices: H(3,3) has no K4, and an adjacent pair has exactly one common neighbor, which together exclude induced minimum degree at least three on at most five vertices. Thus 6p<=27 gives p<=4. The explicit partition {1}x[3]x[3] and {2,3}x{j}x[3] for j=1,2,3 has induced degrees 4,3,3,3 and gives p>=4. Exact exhaustive code checks all 101583 subsets of sizes one through five and independently verifies the partition.
